text:
customer-jane: Hi — after yesterday's DC network maintenance our Private deployment (prod-vpc-3) lost connectivity to Redwood. App calls to the private endpoint start failing with TLS handshake errors and some 502s. This started ~09:12 UTC. Can you help?

support-tyler: Sorry you're hit, Jane. Do you have a short curl + error output and a traceroute/tcpdump from a host in the VPC? Also which peering type — IPsec VPN, Direct Connect, or ExpressRoute?

customer-jane: We're on an IPsec site-to-site (customer-managed ASA) to Redwood Private via Direct Connect fallback. Curl:```curl -v https://private.redwood.example/api/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'```Error: "SSL_connect: ssl handshake failure" then HTTP 502 on retries.
I attached a quick tcpdump from an app host (port 443):```18:45:12.123456 IP 10.12.5.3.443 > 35.190.11.9.53412: Flags [P.], seq 1:517, ack 1, win 229, length 516
18:45:12.125000 IP 10.12.5.3 > 35.190.11.9: ICMP 59 fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)
18:45:12.125200 IP 35.190.11.9.53412 > 10.12.5.3.443: Flags [S.], seq 12345, ack 1, win 29200, options [mss 1460], length 0```

networking-luke: Thanks — that ICMP "fragmentation needed" is a big clue. Which MTU is configured on the IPsec tunnel and on the Direct Connect interface? MTU mismatch + DF can break TLS stacks that don't handle PMTUD well. Also confirm NAT-T (UDP 4500) allowed and ESP (proto 50) not blocked by any intermediate firewall.

support-tyler: Also can you paste the BGP/peering status from the customer edge device and from the VPC router? Even if BGP is up, asymmetric path + MTU can still cause TLS breaks.

customer-jane: CE shows BGP Established to our router, but on the Redwood side the VPC route table shows occasional route withdraws (we saw flapping around 09:10-09:16). I don't have the Redwood side logs. MTU on CE is 1500, we set tunnel interface to 1500.

oncall-bot: @support escalation created: INC-2026-4923 — assigned to networking-luke and sre-jordan.

networking-luke: Quick checklist while you pull logs: 1) Confirm IPsec mode is route-based (VTI) not policy-based if you expect larger packets. 2) Ensure DF/PMTUD is allowed through appliances. 3) Check if tunnel interface MTU should be lowered (common fix: 1400 for IPsec over Direct Connect). 4) Ensure UDP 500/4500 and ESP allowed egress and ingress on all firewalls/NATs. 5) If using NAT on the CE, ensure NAT traversal/NAT-T is enabled.

sre-jordan: On the Redwood side I can see corresponded BGP flaps for that customer during the maint window — likely transient route churn. I also see a spike in TLS handshake errors from our side for that VPC. Jordan: can you test connectivity to the customer's public peer IP 54.201.12.34 from our edge?

eng-ops: Quick reproduction command we use:```# from an app host inside VPC
traceroute -n -F -p 4500 54.201.12.34
# tcpdump filter we ask for
tcpdump -i eth0 host 54.201.12.34 or port 4500 or proto 50 -w /tmp/peer.pcap
```This will show NAT-T packets + ESP.

customer-jane: We lowered tunnel MTU to 1400 and enabled NAT-T on the ASA. After a few minutes the handshake errors dropped to near zero and the 502 rate returned to normal. Confirming: was the fix MTU or the NAT-T change?

networking-luke: Both likely contributed. That ICMP "fragmentation needed" indicates PMTUD failure; lowering MTU removes need for fragmentation. If NAT was blocking UDP 4500/ESP then NAT-T/ESP issues could have forced fragmentation or dropped packets. We'll keep monitoring.

support-tyler: Closing loop for you: we've left INC-2026-4923 open for 48h for monitoring. Recommended postmortem actions for your infra: 1) Keep tunnel MTU at 1400 for tunnels over Direct Connect/MPLS. 2) Ensure firewall rules allow ESP (proto 50) and UDP 500/4500 end-to-end. 3) Enable PMTUD-friendly configs (allow ICMP type 3 code 4). 4) Consider enabling MSS clamping on your edge NAT if you see repeat PMTUD signs. 5) Share config if you want a review.

customer-jane: Thanks all — rolling change looks stable. Appreciate the quick help :heart:

sre-jordan: We'll also add a KB snippet to the Private onboarding docs about MTU/NAT-T best practices for IPsec over Direct Connect.

support-tyler: Marking thread resolved after 48h with no regressions. If anything reappears ping here or reopen INC-2026-4923.
